title: Systematic Theology: An Introduction to Biblical Doctrine
author: Wayne Grudem
description: Church discipline is essential to building a healthy church. Facing the endless variety of complex circumstances and sins that lack direct scriptural case studies, local congregations require a clear, biblical framework to administer correction appropriately in love. Jonathan Leeman provides a contemporary, concise, and practical how-to guide that equips leaders and believers with a deep theological understanding of disciplinary measures. Through real-life situations and practical responses, this volume offers actionable wisdom for establishing a faithful, thriving community. It serves as a definitive guide to exercising Christian responsibility, love, and discipline within the local church.

title: The Christ of the Covenants
author: O. Palmer Robertson
description: A comprehensive study showing how covenant theology unifies the overarching redemptive message of both Old and New Testaments. Robertson carefully examines the administration of God's covenant of grace through history, pointing ultimately to Christ as the fulfillment of all divine promises.

title: The Epistle to the Romans (New International Commentary)
author: Douglas J. Moo
description: An exhaustive, highly regarded exegetical commentary unpacking Paul's letter to the Romans verse by verse. Douglas Moo interacts deeply with historical theology, Greek text structures, and the core theological arguments concerning justification by faith alone.

title: Instruments in the Redeemer's Hands
author: Paul David Tripp
description: People growing in Christ change through daily personal ministry. This book helps every Christian become an instrument of change. True practical change happens when we understand that God uses everyday people in the body of Christ to speak His truth in love, helping one another navigate life's brokenness under the Gospel.

title: Christian Ethics: Contemporary Issues and Options
author: Norman L. Geisler
description: An overview of major ethical systems evaluated through a traditional evangelical and biblical framework. Geisler presents structured approaches to complex moral dilemmas facing modern believers, anchoring absolute truth in the unchanging character of God.

title: The Pilgrim's Progress
author: John Bunyan
description: The timeless Christian allegory depicting the trials, temptations, and triumphs of the believer's journey to the Celestial City. As Christian flees the City of Destruction, every obstacle he encounters reflects the spiritual reality of Christian perseverance.
